name: English as a Second Language ESL Level 4
subject: English As a Second Language and English Literacy Development
subject_group: English As a Second Language and English Literacy Development
description: This course prepares students to use English with increasing fluency and accuracy in classroom and social situations and to participate in Canadian society as informed citizens. Students will develop the oral-presentation, reading, and writing skills required for success in all school subjects. They will extend listening and speaking skills through participation in discussions and seminars; study and interpret a variety of grade-level texts; write narratives, articles, and summaries in English; and respond critically to a variety of print and media texts.

elaborations.text: What visual clues are used to identify ‘good’ and ‘bad’ characters in movies and music videos you have seen recently?

specific_expectations.text: demonstrate understanding that different media texts may reflect different points of view, and suggest reasons why particular perspectives are presented (e.g., marketing concerns may influence whether media texts include or ignore people of a particular age, gender, income level, or ethnocultural background; news reports of a conflict may present more than one point of view to try to achieve the “balance” appropriate for a general audience)

elaborations.text: Whose point of view is most often presented in media texts? Why? Who is often absent from advertising in magazines and on television?

specific_expectations.text: create a variety of media texts for specific purposes and audiences (e.g., a news report summarizing the causes and potential consequences of a current issue such as Aboriginal land claims; an editorial to explain and support a position on an issue; an interview with a person with a physical disability about barriers and access in public places for publication in a school or community magazine/newspaper; a public-service announcement on a current issue relevant to students such as poverty, AIDS, violence prevention, or global warming)
